claims.rationale: Exact local bytes, deterministic tests, package identities, and accepted structural evidence support the scoped self-consistency claim, while semantic independence, measured learning value, controller enforcement, and release lifecycle outcomes remain separate unobserved gates.
claims.statement: On this Windows host, analyze-project-claims applied its own accepted component-map and evidence-bound protocol to the local v0.9.0 candidate. The exact accepted map passed an unchanged reconciliation and preflight; the package, embedded engine, and official skill validator verified; 262 of 263 repository tests passed with one privilege-dependent symlink skip; and twenty-three focused tests validated the closed digest-bound evaluation manifest/result contract, distinct exact-receipt and frozen-taxonomy binding, exact repetition binding, recomputed gates, direct-failure precedence, malformed-input rejection, and state-free validation. This establishes local structural self-consistency only: no representative pilot, pinned model evaluation, quality improvement, independent implementation, trusted repair controller, release, installation, or activation was observed.

The repository used the same analyzer package, evidence engine, schemas, and recorder to audit its own candidate, so this is deterministic self-consistency evidence rather than independent validation.

limitations.text: Closed manifest/result schemas and deterministic tests do not authenticate observations or establish representative pilot reproducibility, false-cluster rate, owner cost, model quality lift, or absence of regression.

The self-audit reuses the analyzer package, component-evidence engine, schemas, and recorder under test; it is not an independent implementation or scientific replication and may share semantic defects.
Local tests and accepted-map preflight do not prove a trusted repair controller, commit-bound CI, release publication, managed installation, client routing, or fresh activation.
